newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Baltic Shipping to cut staff.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Shipping to cut staff.

text.p: Baltic Shipping will solve its financial problems partly by cutting staff, a senior government official told Reuters on Tuesday.
Boris Grishin, first deputy head of the Federal Maritime Shipping Service, refused to mention how many employees of the company, AO Baltiiskoye Morskoye Parokhodstvo (BMP), would be laid off.
More than 10,000 of the shipping company's employees have filed suits to a local court against wage arrears. At some ships staff have not received wages for four to five months.
The maritime shipping service had applied to the finance ministry to grant BMP a credit to pay taxes to unfreeze accounts, Grishin said.
"The letter is already in the finance ministry," he told Reuters. "This is a credit for the amount of taxes owed and an application to defer payment for six months."
This month BMP sold one ship to cover wage debts and plans to sell a further two ships at an auction in November.

The government, which already owns 29.7 percent of Baltic Shipping, is seeking to take a controlling stake in the troubled company, which posted 215.82 billion roubles in losses in 1995, according to Russian accounting standards.
The company's total debt to foreign creditors exceeds $300 million and many of its ships have been seized in foreign ports.
